utterances.text: And you also said that a man had beaten you with a baseball bat; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you describe a baseball bat to us.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was made of wood. It was short. A bit on the thick side. About this long. I also think that it had a hole on the top and there was something going through that hole. Now, was it a rope or was it a leather string, I don't know. Something that you held in your hand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that the man who had beaten you was a member of the army. Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you also said that he had been involved in mopping up tasks in Mahala; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so. That's my assumption. Because while he was there -- while I was there, he was taking water, was threatening me, and he said it himself. I cannot remember all his words with great precision. He assaulted me then. Something else. As a matter of fact, I think that on that day, right after that, when I was already taken into the cell, somebody - either him or somebody else - threw something at the cell window, which had metal all around it. And he said that he was throwing a grenade. We were afraid, we who were inside. This happened twice within two or three minutes' time. Fortunately nothing happened. It was not a grenade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Again, Judge, may I remind you to try and answer the question and nothing else. The question was: "And you also said that he had been involved in ethnic cleansing in Mahala; is that correct?" So the answer is either yes or no, and you said "I think so. That's my assumption."

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, Mr. President. I think that there is a problem with the translation. It concerns the word "nettoyage," which in fact means "cleaning up."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, "nettoyage," is cleaning up, but the translation that I had and also in the transcript it's ethnic cleansing.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. But that's not what I said. Exactly. I was speaking about --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Judge, we are not talking about ethnic cleansing. These are things that happen in this Trial Chamber shifting from one language to another. Madam Fauveau is asking you or asked you whether you -- you still stand by your previous statement that this person was also involved in the cleaning up of Mahala where your residence was.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes. The way I had put it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You stand by that statement. Madam Fauveau, yes, please. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know that this man was a member of the army?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: By his military uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say a military uniform, could you describe this military uniform.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Camouflage uniform, military. I remember that he had a beard, glasses -- sunglasses. He had short gloves on his hands, short leather gloves without the top part of the fingers on the gloves. I think that I knew that person. I think that I knew him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you identify him?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I can.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us his name?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the name. But as for the last name, I think it was Stupar. I also think that he was an electric technician by training.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who was involved in the cleaning up in Mahala?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, may I just -- I'm now a bit unclear. Clearly what the judge was talking about was ethnic cleansing. Is what Madam Fauveau talking about ethnic cleansing? That's the trouble with this translation. But if you look at the -- I checked on the original answer, and it's clear that the suggestion was that this man was involved in the ethnic cleansing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The question was, as put in the transcript -- yes, it was like that. But I think she's corrected it --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I know. But it's very --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: She didn't correct it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It's unclear by using the word in French, "nettoyage," is Madam Fauveau talking about cleaning up as in cleaning lavatories or cleaning as in cleaning out people, which is ethnic cleansing?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Perhaps, Madam Fauveau, you could make that clear. It is clear to me after having brought it up myself -- or after you brought it up, actually. But perhaps you could clarify this for us once and for all. And then I will ask the judge, the witness, if he has anything to add or change to his evidence. What do you mean by "nettoyage" in the context of the questions you have been putting to the witness, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When I mention cleaning, I'm talking about the sanitation of the terrain in Mahala. And what the word "nettoyage" in French means is that it doesn't mean ethnic cleansing when you use this word in French.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Judge, you have heard -- I suppose the translation -- the interpretation has already been done. You've heard what Madam Fauveau has just explained. And I repeat the question that Madam Fauveau had put to you, whether you stand by your previous -- by your alleged previous statement that this particular person that beat you up with the short baseball bat was also involved in the -- I'm going to use the word now that has been interpreted -- sanitation process of Mahala or whether you meant something else.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I stand by my statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Yes, Madam Fauveau, you may proceed, please. Thank you. Is that clear enough for you, Ms. Korner, now?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll clarify the matter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us who was involved in the cleaning up in Mahala in the sense of sanitising the terrain?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sanitising the terrain? At that time I was in prison. But what I learned was that in sanitising the terrain, the work brigade took part -- or rather, the work team of the public utility enterprise of Sanski Most, where they -- where there were workers, gypsies and Bosniaks. That is what has to do with the -- with sanitising the terrain, because that's what you asked me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you confirm that the army was not involved in this sanitisation process of the terrain?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to what I knew and what I found out, the army took part in the ethnic cleansing of Mahala, in the demolition of Mahala, torching Mahala, expelling the population. That's what the army did. And it was the 6th Krajina Brigade at that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll return to this matter later. Right now I'm talking about the sanitisation of the terrain.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. I think Madam Fauveau is going to have to actually spell out in clear terms what she means by "sanitisation," because at the moment there's real -- the witness is saying expelling people, burning houses, and so forth. I'm not at all clear, and I don't think he is, what Madam Fauveau means [Realtime transcript read in error "Dominican Republic"] by the term she's using.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think it was explained last week by the witness himself. But I perfectly agree that perhaps you could ask the question directly, what you mean by sanitation -- sanitisation process of Mahala and whether the witness is meaning the same thing. I mean, you did give evidence last week on also by reference to some documents that were shown to you to the sanitisation process in some areas. Is this what you are referring to? In other words, the clearing up of the terrain from dead bodies or remains of persons, of corpses? And is this what you mean by the word, Madam Fauveau? Because you can't possibly have a situation where you're talking at cross-purposes. Could you explain to the witness, please, in your own words relating -- with reference to your question what you mean by "sanitisation process," something that you referred to as cleaning, nettoyage, earlier on?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour. Before Madam Fauveau explains --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Your microphone, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Before --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Again, your microphone.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'll start again. On the screen, I appear to have said "I'm not at all clear and I don't think he is what Madam Fauveau is Dominican Republic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I see it. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, I don't remember what I said, but I certainly can't have said that. Does anyone have the faintest idea. Because this is the trouble. One tries to go back through the note that comes out to make these corrections, but sometimes it's impossible to work out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Let's start with that. You did not mention at any time the Dominican Republic, Madam Fauveau, did you?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It was me. Not her

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It wasn't me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. But you did not mention.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I didn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Neither did you.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, for once it wasn't me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So now my question: Could you please explain to the witness in your own words and also to the Trial Chamber what you meant by "sanitisation process."

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I could just ask the registrar to show -- show the witness document P643.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When I talk about the cleaning up of the terrain in Mahala or the sanitisation of the terrain, I'm referring to what is noted in this document in paragraph 2. And my question to the witness was: Was the army involved in this work?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The army took part in the attack. As for the sanitisation, what His Honour asked about, I already said that a work unit took part. I don't know whether they were attached to the municipal staff or the civilian defence or -- but it was workers of the public utility enterprise for sure. And among them were the Roma who worked in the public utility enterprise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Now, Judge, just to clarify this whole incident now once and for all, my question to you is: So when you were previously asked by Madam Fauveau whether the person that beat you up with the baseball bat, that you think was known as Stupar or -- Stupar and who you said was also a member of the military, whether he was involved in the sanitisation process -- in other words, the removal of bodies -- in the Mahala or whether he was involved in some other kind of cleansing when you made that statement, what did you mean when you previously last week stated that this particular individual, this person, was involved in the cleansing of Mahala? Did you mean the -- ethnic cleansing or did you mean the sanitisation process?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I meant that this person took part in ethnic cleansing. That is to say, in the attack on Mahala and in expelling the population from Mahala, because no one remained in Mahala. There were only ruins there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I think that clarifies the issue for you as well, Madam Fauveau. And possibly you may proceed to another question.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would nevertheless like to clarify a point since at the hearing of the 25th of April -- on page 4979 of the French transcript -- the witness stated: That man -- and was speaking about the person with the baseball bat -- that man worked or carried out sanitisation work because he had gloves in Mahala -- he had gloves without fingers -- the finger parts had been cut off. I would like to know how such a description could be used for a person who was carrying out ethnic cleansing. This description corresponds exactly to a person who is involved in the sanitisation of the terrain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This is the sitting of 25th of April?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The 25th of April. Page 4979 in the French transcript. Unfortunately I don't have it in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... but it goes on to say: "He wore glasses and he was in uniform. I think his name is Stupar."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Judge, I am going to read out to you what, according to the transcript, you said to us during the 49th sitting, that is on the 25th of April. You are reported here to have said the following: Question: "And finally just before we have the break, did the person who hit you with the baseball bat, what was he? What was his job?" And you answered: "This man, I think, was cleaning the Mahala, because he wore black gloves with the fingers cut off. He wore glasses and he was in uniform. I think his name is Stupar." Then there was a further question: "Okay. I'm sorry to stop you. But was that -- was he a policeman, a military policeman -- or a military or an ordinary policeman -- military police or ordinary military?" And you answered: "He was from the military. I don't know whether he was a military policeman." And that's when we then had the break, soon after that. So I think that Madam Fauveau's question is pretty much in order. What did the fact that you saw this man, military or not military is not that important for the time being -- wearing gloves, black gloves, with the fingers -- half mittens, we call them -- with the fingers cut off mean to you? And how and why did you relate it to some kind of cleaning of the Mahala that you referred to in your evidence on that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When he saw me, he knew I was from Mahala, and he mentioned this. He said, "We've done away with Mahala," and he was cussing and things like that. As a matter of fact, when I returned to the cell, I talked about that to the other prisoners.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But you've still not answered my question. Usually when I see someone wearing half mittens, I get the impression that that person may have bad circulation or that he needs to keep his hands warm while he is working. That's what I associate the wearing of half mittens with, someone who needs to keep his hands warm while at the same time having the tips of the finger free. Now, you're saying that this man was wearing black gloves with the fingers cut off, and you seem to be associating this with the cleaning of Mahala. Why would you or anyone else associate the wearing of black half mittens with the cleaning of Mahala? What does wearing black gloves with the fingers cut off have to do with the cleaning of Mahala at a time when I suppose you were not referring to the removal of the dead bodies?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These gloves, they are a special type. They're used for handling weapons. And there were such persons who were in these units. I'm not linking him up with the gloves. I'm saying what I heard. He said this himself. I mean when I got back to the cell, some of the persons who were in the cell told me everything about him. I think that this policeman, the one who escorted me to the cell, told me that he had just returned. I mean, it was a long time ago. It's hard to remember all these details. But please do not link the gloves with that, because it was military policemen who had these gloves, all of them more or less who were involved in these actions, these armed actions, that is. It has nothing to do with what the lady -- the Defence counsel asked me about. It has nothing to do with this sanitation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, Your Honours may want to look at the evidence of Mr. -- Mr. Dzonlic who gave evidence about these types of gloves as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. But the person who is giving evidence is the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But now I think it's pretty clear enough that if he's referring to gloves, strictly military gloves -- I have gloves like those, for example, which I use for driving sometimes. But it's -- Yes, Madam Fauveau, if you want to put further questions on this particular incident, you may. But I think it's clear enough, and I suggest you move to something else.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have one other question concerning this man.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you know that this man was a member of the army and not a member of the SOS forces or of the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: His military uniform, first and foremost. I also heard about him from other prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would it perhaps be a good time to have a break? Because I'm going to move on to another subject.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Certainly, Madam Fauveau. We'll now have a break, again for 30 minutes, resuming at five to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I just apologise for keeping Your Honours waiting. I'm afraid that I wasn't aware that the time had gone on like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Ms. Korner, thank you. Yes, Madam Fauveau. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the hearing of the 25th of April, on page 4988 -- you said that a group of policemen and soldiers made you go out to see what was happening in Mahala on the 27th of May in the afternoon. Do you remember this?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on page 89 -- 4989 at the same date, you said this group on the 25th of May came at 5.00 in the morning. Could you explain this -- these differences.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not what I said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll quote here. It's on page 4989 of the French transcript, line 10. "As I said, at 5.00 in the morning on the 27th of May, a policeman arrived and he opened the door to the cell. He was armed and he was accompanied by several other persons."

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One policeman, yes. One policeman who opened the door.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you leave the prison and police station on the 27th of May in the morning or in the afternoon in order to see what was happening in Mahala?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They took us out of the cells in the afternoon. It was a large group of policemen and soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the same page, 4989, on the 25th of April you said that these soldiers who were in this group were the ones, the soldiers, who had been in Mahala. At the time that the soldiers were in Mahala, you were in prison; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you personally were not able to see these soldiers in Mahala; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said on page 4997 that the members of the 6th Brigade destroyed the mosque. Is it true that at the time the mosque was destroyed, you were in prison?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you personally did not see the destruction -- you did not see the mosque being destroyed.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the hearing of the 16th of May, you spoke about the destruction of a mosque in November 1992. I think that was in the village of Sehovci, the village in which your sister lived.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You personally did not see this destruction; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the registrar show the witness documents DT11 and DT10.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you look at document DT10. It's an order from General Talic. And the date is the 23rd of June, 1992. Is it true that in the first paragraph of this order, General Talic forbids the destruction of religious buildings -- the destruction and the damaging of religious buildings?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you asking me? Ask him. I know that the buildings were destroyed, all of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that in the first paragraph of this order, the destruction and damaging of mosques is forbidden?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the first paragraph, what it says it says. But this is pro forma.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you read what is written in the first paragraph.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You want me to read it? You can read it too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Judge, please read the first paragraph and then you may be asked questions upon it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I'm not sure what questions he can be asked. We've seen the document before. We know the order. What's he supposed to say about it unless he saw it before?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Well, we'll see what questions Madam Fauveau has afterwards.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But he's been -- it -- I mean, as -- the judge should know that what is -- what is a regular question and what is not regular. I mean -- and he is free to then answer the -- in any way he deems fit. And he has already hinted as what he thinks about this particular document. But I do have to accept Madam Fauveau's request.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I can't read this. This is hypocritical.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I'm sorry. We've read it. Why read it aloud? Unless he's seen this order before, where are we going to get to with this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Did you ever see this document before, Judge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's the first time you're seeing it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I can't remember. Probably. I haven't read all of it now either. I've just read the first paragraph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So read it all, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if it's easier for the witness, I'll ask the question again, if he wants to reply to it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that General Talic forbade the destruction and the infliction of damage on mosques? If he can answer this question, it won't be necessary for him to read this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That, I think he has already answered. He told you that it says what it says, but that he considers it as hypocritical.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. But when he say that is the document states what it states, that doesn't mean either yes or no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you agree, Judge, that on the face of it this document in paragraph number 1, numbered number "1," states that General Momir Talic is ordering to ensure at all levels of command that religious buildings or cemeteries of any religion are not desecrated in combat operations or any other situations? Do you agree that in its first numbered paragraph, this statement or this document says precisely what I have read out to you? I have the -- I have the version in English. I don't understand your language. And the question that has been put to you by Madam Fauveau is perfectly in order. Do you agree that this first paragraph says what I read out to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree. I agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Madam Fauveau, next question.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you now have a look at the document DT11. It's a document which was signed by General Talic. Someone signed on his behalf. It's a document from the 1st Krajina Corps command, which again reminds people of the fact that religious buildings should not be destroyed or damaged; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the hearing of the 24th of April -- it's page 4924 -- you spoke about the director of Sanski Most radio who had been forcibly expelled from the radio. Do you remember speaking about this?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you personally present in the radio station when this expulsion took place?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not personally present at the radio station itself, but I got a report as to what had happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you personally didn't see the director of the radio being expelled.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the hearing of the 13th of May, you spoke about a killing that took place in Skrljevita and in which the Croats were the victims. Perhaps that was near Kruhari. And you said on the 13th of May -- it's page 67 of the LiveNote -- that no proceedings had been instituted against the perpetrators of these crimes, against the killers. Do you stand by this statement?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not by the -- not at the court in Sanski Most. I think that a criminal report was filed in the court in Banja Luka. I don't know what happened. During the last five or six months perhaps -- that is to say, as of recent -- the investigating judge at the district court in Banja Luka, Mr. Slobodan Milasinovic, contacted me by telephone, and he asked me whether there were any documents -- or rather, there was a case pertaining to the perpetrators of that crime. I assume that perhaps proceedings have been instituted and are taking place right now before the court in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the registrar show the witness document DT12 and DT13.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Now, Judge, if this is the first time you are seeing these two documents, I will give you time to have a look at them before I authorise Madam Fauveau to put questions to you.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I direct the witness to look at document DT12 first of all, the document which is an indictment.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the first time I have seen this indictment, and I don't know when it was issued.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the Serbo-Croat version that I have here, the date can't be read. But in the English version, the date is the 2nd of June, 1993.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's possible. But I wonder if anybody has been actually convicted. Last time I talked about this I said that, and I said that to the best of my knowledge nobody was convicted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The question which was put to you on the 13th of May -- it's page 67 of the LiveNote -- the question was: [In English] "Do you know whether a trial ever took place?" [Interpretation] And your reply was: [In English] "No, never."

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if there was a trial, because the indictment on its own doesn't say anything to me. If you have a decision, a judgement, that's different.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I think again we better be careful. If -- is Madam Fauveau suggesting that an actual trial, as opposed to -- because there's no question prosecution was commenced. But the question of trial --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Is the suggestion to the judge that an actual trial, a hearing and a sentence took place?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: For the time being, Ms. Korner, I understand that the direction of the question that she has asked was to establish whether the witness was as categoric as he pretended to be when he gave evidence on the 22nd of May -- or whenever you said he gave it.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the 13th of May.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Previouos translation continues] ... of the actual official transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And in actual fact, if she is -- I don't have the transcript here in front of me. But if she is right in quoting what the witness said on that occasion and considering the answer that he has given now, she has already established or made at least the first point that she needed or she wanted to make.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No. Your Honour, she left out the beginning part of my question, which makes it clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. But she is -- she can go ahead with asking that question now.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No. Your Honour, you don't understand. The actual full question -- because -- that's what I mean about the definition of a trial. Because my question actually reads -- I said: "From your investigations, was he ever prosecuted, brought to trial, or serve any sentence? And I then said I'll then rephrase that because that's three questions rolled into one. First of all, we see that a prosecution was launched in respect of these matters. Then do you know whether or not a trial actually took place?" So that what I mean. You --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And his answer on that occasion was?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: "No, never." But that's what I mean. It's misleading the way it was put.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You are right now. I have it clear now. So the question ought to be whether he stands by that previous statement of his, that to his knowledge there was never a trial -- a trial to the ordinary sense of the word as we understand it in our environment.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That was my understanding of this word.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Are you aware whether a trial took place or not? In other words, do you stand by your previous statement that there -- to your knowledge there was never any such trial?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I know, there was never any such trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No one was ever convicted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I got the impression earlier on when we started on this incident that you were hinting that there may be some proceedings pending now. Am I right, or did I get you wrong?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You are quite right. You are quite right. The court in Banja Luka asked me for information, and I have the feeling that the trial is taking place right now against these persons, right now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. So that clarifies more or less the picture. Yes, Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this document, DT12, which you have in front of you, it is an indictment concerning the killing in Skrljevita; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are persons from Skrljevita, and the killing was in Kruhari. That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Is it correct that the indictment can be addressed according to Yugoslav law after the investigation has been accomplished? So an indictment can be compiled after an investigation has been accomplished. After an investigation has been accomplished?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that's the way it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And according to Yugoslav law, the investigation procedure is part of the process, of the criminal process.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So as this process of trial was engaged in 1992 and 1993; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether an investigation was carried out there at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How according to Yugoslav law could an indictment be issued if the investigation hadn't been carried out and if this concerned a crime that had been described as aggravated murder?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether there was an investigation here at all. This was conducted by the military court and the office of the military prosecutor. And shall I say of the Serb army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you have a look at the first paragraph concerning the motives, the first sentence which relates to the investigation.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is mentioned, but I don't know whether it was actually carried out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that the Penal Code requires that the investigation procedure, which is obligatory for crimes of aggravated murder be carried out?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Law on Criminal Procedure does provide for that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you have a look at document DT13. It's a decision from the military court in Banja Luka. And once again, the Serbo-Croat version is very bad. And in the English version, the date is the 9th of July, 1993. Do you agree that this is a decision that concerns detention?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't read it, because the copy is not a good one. Have you got another copy?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I have the copy that I was provided with by the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I'm afraid there isn't a better copy. It was taken from the court records, and that was the best we could do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Judge, I have the same copy that you have. As I see it, if you divide this page into two parts, the second part which starts after the word [B/C/S spoken], the next two or three or four paragraphs, with the exception of a few letters here and there are legible. I don't know whether yours is exactly like mine, your text, the one that you have, but with the exception as I see, there are only a few letters, and for anyone who knows the language, I don't think they are such that would make a difference except maybe in the third paragraph, the one which has only got a line and a half. Otherwise, if you perhaps could make an effort, you should be able to provide Defence counsel with an answer. Forget about the first part, because there -- I agree there are lines which are absolutely illegible. But the substantive part of the document -- in other words, where there is the statement of reasons, you should be able to read.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can confirm that -- or rather, I can answer that question. The decision and the statement of reasons shows that it does have to do with detention for Danilusko Kajtez and for Milos Maksimovic [phoen].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We're talking of pre-trial confinement -- pre-trial detention custody pending trial; correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think there is a problem with the translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. It is not the first or last time we are encountering this problem.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness quite clearly said that it was a decision for pre-trial detention, and I don't think that this appears in the English translation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes. Pre-trial detention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes. Next question.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You spoke about two transports to Manjaca, on the 6th and on the 12th of June. And you said that on each occasion, six persons disappeared. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In one transport, six; in the other transport, six. A total of 12 in these two transports.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 6th and 12th of June, 1992, you were personally in the police station in Sanski Most; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in prison, in the prison of the public security station in Sanski Most.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You weren't present when these lorries were transporting the people; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You spoke about Hivzo Hodzic, who was the president of the SDA in Sanski Most. And you said that he had been killed on the 17th of July, 1992 while he was in the transport to Manjaca; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was on the 7th of July.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're right. It was on the 7th of July.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at the time, you were already in Manjaca; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were not personally present when this -- when these lorries were transporting the people.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were personally transported to Manjaca, who were the guards accompanying you?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From Sanski Most towards Manjaca?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Drago Vujanic was there. He was the commander of the prison at that time. He has a degree in law. Then there was Zoran Despot. He is a crime investigation inspector from the public security station. And I saw the two of them, and they took me out of jail. And I saw them from the back in the police car, and they escorted us to Manjaca. And at Manjaca, Vujanic was calling us out from the truck, telling us to jump off. I didn't see anybody else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were being transported to Manjaca, was there anyone among the prisoners who was killed?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody was killed in my transport.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was there anyone among the prisoners who died during this transport?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already said that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I assume that the answer is no.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that the commander of the Manjaca camp was someone called Popovic.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was that person's last name. His first name was Bozidar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you said that this person called Popovic was familiar with the situation in the Manjaca camp.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether this Popovic informed his superior of the situation in Manjaca?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the registrar show the witness document DT13 -- DT3. [In English] DT3.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Is this a document that we were notified about? Because we don't seem to have it here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] We don't have it --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Oh, I know. Yes. It's a drawing of Manjaca. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Document DT3. It's my fault, Mr. President. The document is DT2. Perhaps we could put it on the ELMO, since you don't have it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, you can hand the witness the B/C/S version and put the English one on the ELMO, because the map -- or the sketch, the drawing of the camp, we have. But that's -- I understand now is not -- not the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: That's what we've got it down as, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And Madam Fauveau, you have not more than three or four minutes to conclude. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you agree that this is an order from General Talic dated the 7th of June, 1992?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is what it says here. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it also says in the last paragraph, paragraph 3: "It is necessary to behave towards the prisoners in a dignified and humane way, without attacking them. They must not be insulted, and they must not be frightened. They should be provided with medical care. The sick should be provided with medical care and with accommodation according to the rules of international war" -- is that correct -- "according to the rules of international war law."

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I'm asking you what is written in paragraph 3. Or if you prefer, you could read this paragraph.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says, the way you said it. However --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you have a look at page 2 of this document. Among the addressees of this order, you can find Manjaca too.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see Manjaca anywhere. Yes. Yes, it says "Manjaca training ground." Yes, Manjaca training ground.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Manjaca training ground. I don't know what they meant by "training ground," because its diameter was 40 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So that brings us to the end of today's session. We will resume tomorrow morning at 9.00 sharp. The witness can be escorted out. Thank you, Judge. We will meet again tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I've just got one matter before we forget about it and we move along too far. I raised last week sometime the question of the -- Mr. Dzonlic's documents, and I still haven't had a response whether it's accepted or whether I need to put them in as an exhibit. That is those letters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Ackerman needed some time.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I'd be quite grateful so we can deal with it before we get far away from it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I promise we'll have an opportunity to deal with it before this case ends, Your Honour, quite a lot sooner than that, Your Honour. We do need to get through them.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: There's only seven, Your Honour. So I really would like an answer by the end of this week [The witness stands down].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, judge. We'll deal with it before the end of this week in one way or another. Thank you. We'll all meet tomorrow morning at 9.00. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
